_about: Fidelity ratchet baseline for the byte-exact decompilation (docs/fidelity_ratchet.md).
Every site listed here is GRANDFATHERED: it exists in the tree today and does not
block anything.  tools/integrate.py and tools/overlay_land_function.py refuse a
landing only when it ADDS a blocking-class site to the row being landed; a site that
DISAPPEARS never blocks (that is the burn-down).  Regeneration is explicit
(--write-baseline / --prune-baseline), never automatic -- same rule as
config/portability_baseline.json.
BLOCKING: LABEL_AS_CALL, PASSTHRU_NO_ARGS (both readable off the candidate C text).
DEBT (never blocks): PASSTHRU, INDIRECT_PASSTHRU (byte-derived -- a CORRECT C still
produces them), JT_KEEP_ORDER (from jtbl_verify.py; not evaluated at landing time).
Site id = <CLASS>|<target>|<ordinal within the row>, never a line number.
COUNTED BUT NOT REFUSED (still real debt, still listed here, still burnt down like
any other site; only the LANDING answer differs): a LABEL_AS_CALL the candidate C
registers as a zero-arg noreturn tail jump ('noreturn-tail') or as an authenticated
per-site maspsx SHAPE-D sibcall pin ('shape-d-pin').  The two carry SEPARATE labels
in the per-site JSON (decomp_audit.py --json) so a burn-down can never merge them;
an epilogue label qualifies for neither.
Override an intended regression with --allow-fidelity-regression or
AZ_ALLOW_FIDELITY_REGRESSION=1, then re-run --write-baseline.
KEYED BY ROW IDENTITY: <container>/<func_vram>, the extractor's synthetic name,
which is unique inside a container and does NOT move under an identity sweep.  Each
record carries the row's true_name for readability only -- never as a key.  (Before
2026-08-24 the key was <container>/<true_name or func_vram>; a bare true name is a
RAM-SLOT LABEL, not an identity, so 10 renamed rows silently inherited another row's
grandfathered sites.  A baseline without the key_scheme field below is that old one;
the landing hook disables itself on it rather than refusing every renamed row.)

_: The whole-tree regen re-measured every row from its LANDED TU.  Six BLOCKING sites
that entered the tree between the 2026-08-24 regen and today with no sanctioned
route (no counted-not-refused shape, no sibling-bank precedent) are deliberately
WITHHELD from the grandfathered set below: they exist in the tree, they are NOT in
this baseline, and a landing that re-adds them is refused.  That is the fail-closed
direction -- do not 'fix' it with --write-baseline; burn the sites down instead
(respell the tail as goto/return), then regenerate.
--prune-baseline both re-measure this set against the tree and keep withholding
each site until it is GONE, then release it loudly as a burn-down.
